chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Qalanisi, from Ali ibn Hassan, from his uncle Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, when Adam (peace be upon him) was sent down to the earth, he was sent down upon al-Safa. It is for that reason that al-Safa was named as such, because al-Mustafa (the Chosen One) descended upon it, and the hill was given a name derived from the name of Adam.
God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Indeed, God chose Adam and Noah and the family of Ibrahim and the family of Imran above the worlds' [3:33].

And Hawwa (Eve) was sent down upon al-Marwa. Al-Marwa was named 'Marwa' because the woman (al-mar'a) descended upon it, and the hill was given a name derived from the name of the woman. They are two hillocks to the right and left of the Ka'ba.

So Adam said, when he was separated from Hawwa: 'Nothing would have separated me from my wife except that she has become forbidden to me.' So he kept away from her, but he would visit her during the day and converse with her. When night came, he feared his soul would overcome him regarding her, so he returned and spent the night upon al-Safa. It is for that reason that women (al-nisa') were named as such, because Adam had no companionship (uns) apart from her.

So Adam remained in that state for as long as God willed him to remain. God neither spoke to him nor sent him a messenger, while the Lord, Glorified be He, boasted of his patience to the angels. When the time arrived that God, Mighty and Majestic, intended to accept Adam's repentance, He sent Jibrail (peace be upon him) to him. He said: 'Peace be upon you, O Adam, you who are patient in your tribulation, repentant from your sin! God, Mighty and Majestic, has sent me to you to teach you the rites by which God intends to accept your repentance.'

So Jibrail (peace be upon him) took Adam (peace be upon him) by the hand until he brought him to the site of the House (Ka'ba). A cloud descended from the sky and shaded the site of the House. Jibrail (peace be upon him) said: 'O Adam! Mark with your foot where the cloud shades, for it is a qibla for you and for the last of your posterity among your children.' So Adam marked with his foot where the cloud shaded.
Then he took him to Mina and showed him the mosque of Mina. He marked with his foot and extended the boundary of the Sacred Mosque after having marked the site of the House.

Then he took him from Mina to Arafat and positioned him at al-Muarraf. He said: 'When the sun sets, acknowledge your sin seven times and ask God for forgiveness and repentance seven times.' Adam (peace be upon him) did that. That is why al-Muarraf was named as such, because Adam acknowledged his sin there. This was established as a sunnah for his children — they acknowledge their sins just as Adam did, and ask for repentance just as Adam asked for it.

Then Jibrail instructed him and he departed from Arafat. He passed by the seven mountains and was instructed to say takbir four times at each mountain. Adam did that until he reached Jam'a (Muzdalifa). When he arrived at Jam'a, a third of the night had passed, and he combined the Maghrib and the last Isha prayers at that place on that third of the night.

Then he instructed him to lie prostrate in the valley of Jam'a, and he lay prostrate in the valley of Jam'a until dawn broke. He then instructed him to ascend the mountain of Jam'a, and when the sun rose, to acknowledge his sin seven times and ask God for repentance and forgiveness seven times. Adam did that just as Jibrail (peace be upon him) had commanded him.

The two acknowledgements were established as a sunnah for his children. Whoever among them does not witness Arafat but reaches Jam'a has fulfilled his Hajj up to Mina. Then he departed from Jam'a to Mina. He reached Mina at mid-morning, and he was instructed to pray two cycles in the mosque of Mina.

Then he instructed him to offer a sacrifice to God, so that it be accepted from him and he would know that God, Mighty and Majestic, had accepted his repentance, and the sacrifice would become a sunnah for his children. So Adam offered a sacrifice and God accepted it from him. He sent a fire from the sky that consumed Adam's sacrifice. Jibrail said to him: 'O Adam! God has bestowed His grace upon you in that He taught you the rites through which He accepts your repentance, and He has accepted your sacrifice. So shave your head in humility before God, Mighty and Majestic, for He has accepted your sacrifice.' So Adam shaved his head in humility before God, Mighty and Majestic.

Then Jibrail took Adam (peace be upon him) by the hand and went with him to the House. Iblis appeared before him at the jamra (stoning site). Iblis, may God curse him, said to him: 'O Adam! Where are you intending to go?' Jibrail (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O Adam! Pelt him with seven pebbles and say takbir with each pebble.' Adam did that and Iblis went away.

Then he appeared before him at the second jamra and said: 'O Adam! Where are you intending to go?' Jibrail (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Pelt him with seven pebbles and say takbir with each pebble.' Adam did that and Iblis went away. Then he appeared before him at the third jamra and said: 'O Adam! Where are you intending to go?' Jibrail (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Pelt him with seven pebbles and say takbir with each pebble.' Adam did that and Iblis went away.

Jibrail (peace be upon him) said to him: 'You will never see him again after your standing here, ever.' Then he took him to the House and instructed him to circumambulate it seven times. Adam did that. Jibrail (peace be upon him) said to him: 'God has forgiven your sin, accepted your repentance, and permitted your wife to you.'

[This hadith is also narrated by] Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr and Ismail ibn Hazim, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abi al-Daylam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similarly.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa — the hill where Adam descended; named after al-Mustafa (the Chosen One)
key_terms.الْجَمْرَة: Al-jamra — the stoning site; where Iblis appeared and was driven away with pebbles
key_terms.الْقُرْبَان: Al-qurban — the sacrifice offered to God, accepted by heavenly fire
key_terms.الْمَرْوَة: Al-Marwa — the hill where Hawwa descended; named after al-mar'a (the woman)
key_terms.الْمَنَاسِك: Al-manasik — the Hajj rites taught by Jibrail to Adam
key_terms.الْمُعَرَّف: Al-Muarraf — the standing place at Arafat; named because Adam acknowledged (i'tirafa) his sin there
key_terms.تَوَاضُع: Tawadu' — humility; the shaving of the head as an act of submission after the accepted sacrifice
key_terms.سُنَّة: Sunnah — established practice; the Hajj rites were established as permanent practice for Adam's descendants

ai.seo_question: What is the origin of the Hajj rites according to Imam al-Sadiq in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the account of Adam and Hawwa's descent to earth, Adam's patient separation from Hawwa, and how Jibrail guided Adam in performing the first ever Hajj as a means of attaining God's forgiveness. The rites of Hajj — including the naming of al-Safa and al-Marwa, the standing at Arafat, the rites of Muzdalifa and Mina, the stoning of Iblis, and the circumambulation of the Ka'ba — are presented as divine institutions established through Adam's primordial experience, forming a sunnah for all his descendants.
